<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 5 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Road to Oz ==

The shaggy man is a wanderer marked by his shaggy attire — a shaggy hat, and later shaggy creamy stockings of silk and shaggy slippers of rose leather with ruby buckles. Upon being brought as a guest into a great hall of a fine palace, he stood holding his shaggy hat, uncertain what would become of him, reflecting that he had perhaps never before been a guest anywhere. Finding himself unexpectedly surrounded by luxury — a bath edged with emeralds as large as door-knobs and water clear as crystal — he gazed upon it all in silent amazement before deciding, in his own wise way, to take advantage of his good fortune.

After dressing in his new finery, the shaggy man admired himself at length in a long mirror. He then discovered a mother-of-pearl chest decorated with silver vines and clustered rubies, engraved with the words "THE SHAGGY MAN: HIS BOX OF ORNAMENTS." Opening the unlocked chest, he found it filled with rich jewels, from which he took a fine golden watch with a large chain, several handsome finger-rings, and a ruby ornament to pin upon the breast of his shaggy shirt-bosom.

=== Events ===

* Dorothy, the shaggy man, Button-Bright, Toto, and Polychrome are stranded at the edge of the Deadly Desert with no way to reach the Land of Oz.
* The shaggy man uses the Love Magnet to summon Johnny Dooit, who quickly builds a sand-boat to carry them across the desert.
* At the Truth Pond, Button-Bright's fox head and the shaggy man's donkey head wash away, restoring their original faces.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 6 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Emerald City of Oz ==

The Shaggy Man travels in the company of Dorothy, the Wizard, Uncle Henry, and Omby Amby. In conversation with the Wizard, he asks about the Fuddles, said to be among the most peculiar people in the Land of Oz, though the Wizard admits he does not know in what way. During a search involving a lost item, he first guesses that a distressed woman has lost her mirror, and is corrected; he later cries out that he has found a queer-shaped piece with a mouth on it, though when tried against an eye and nose the parts do not match.

When a cry for help goes up, the Shaggy Man jumps from the wagon together with the Wizard, Uncle Henry, and Omby Amby to go to a man's assistance, with Dorothy following behind. On another occasion he questions a woman sobbing over the thought that she might have pricked her foot, and elsewhere asks who designed the mansion built for a farmer who wished for land of his own, learning that Jack Pumpkinhead, himself a farmer, had done so.
</div>
